surfaces.name: Web UI and installed PWA served by the Open Session server
Self-hosted Open Session server and opensession CLI (Bun, Linux/macOS/WSL2)
Native Swift app (iOS and macOS, source/TestFlight)

claims.answer: Self-hosted web UI and installed PWA (iOS push needs the installed PWA over HTTPS), macOS Electron shell, native SwiftUI app for iOS 26 and macOS 26 (TestFlight/Xcode), Chrome side-panel extension and the opensession admin CLI; no Android or Windows/Linux desktop client.

scope.plan: Open source (MIT), self-hosted; no hosted plan

desktop_os.answer: Electron shell packaged for macOS arm64 DMG/ZIP; native Swift macOS app (macOS 26.0). No Windows or Linux desktop client; the server runs on Linux, macOS and WSL2 and the browser UI works anywhere.

mobile_apps.answer: Native SwiftUI iOS app (iOS 26.0) built with Xcode or TestFlight workflow; no Android app (no android/kotlin client in packages/clients).

browser.answer: The web UI is served by the server itself and is the required client.

mobile_browser.answer: Web UI installable as a PWA; keyboard and safe-area handling for the installed case; iOS web push requires HTTPS and Home Screen install.

cli.answer: `opensession` CLI covers onboarding, service control, doctor, update, repos, team, runner and automation recipes; session creation and steering are not CLI commands (scripts/cli.ts switch).

editor_extensions.answer: Chrome MV3 side-panel extension captures page context into a session and lists recent sessions; no IDE (VS Code/JetBrains) extension found in packages/clients.

task_actions.answer: Start, steer or queue, answer questions, review and resume sessions in the web UI and native clients; the Chrome extension offers follow-ups with steer/queue but blocking questions open the web UI.

notifications.answer: Web push (opt-in per device), iOS Live Activities and Slack/Linear/GitHub replies.

cross_device_continuity.answer: Sessions live on the server; the same transcript is continued from browser, PWA, desktop shell, native app or extension against one server.

limitations: Electron shell is macOS arm64 only; the Swift app has no public App Store release in the repository (TestFlight workflows, loopback defaults); the CLI administers the server and cannot create or steer sessions; the Chrome extension is not on the Web Store and cannot answer blocking questions.

claims.answer: One embedded harness: the Pi engine runs every model turn in-process, with Anthropic, OpenAI/ChatGPT, xAI (SuperGrok) and OpenAI-compatible providers; no launching of other coding-agent CLIs as harnesses.

scope.plan: Open source (MIT), self-hosted; no hosted plan

harnesses.answer: Only Pi ("Pi is the only production engine"); a bounded search of engine routing found no adapter for other agent CLIs.

model_providers.answer: Anthropic (Claude pool), OpenAI/ChatGPT, xAI SuperGrok, OpenRouter, Cerebras, Wafer and custom OpenAI-compatible providers via model-providers.json.

custom_adapters.answer: Custom OpenAI-compatible providers (protocol openai-completions, base URL, catalog) can be declared; harness adapters are not pluggable by configuration.

session_integration.answer: Embeds the Pi coding-agent runtime in the turn process and controls sessions through its own session kernel and run host protocol.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Only one harness exists; mixed-model sessions (cross-provider fallback with transcript handoff) use the same Pi harness.

limitations: Single harness: model providers vary, but Claude Code, Codex and other agent CLIs are not run as harnesses; the claude and codex CLIs are used for account sign-in.

claims.answer: Bring-your-own Claude subscriptions (setup tokens), ChatGPT sign-ins, SuperGrok sign-ins, OpenAI and other provider API keys, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; pooled with per-person assignment and automatic rotation. No vendor credits because there is no hosted service.

scope.plan: Open source (MIT), self-hosted; no hosted plan

agent_subscriptions.answer: Claude account pool (setup token from `claude setup-token`), ChatGPT sign-ins via in-app device flow and SuperGrok device-code sign-in.

api_accounts.answer: OpenAI API keys in the OpenAI pool and any other provider API key plus base URL under Your own providers.

vendor_credits.answer: Open Session has no hosted service or credit purchase flow; repository, install script and site show only self-hosting (bounded search: README, docs/setup, site).

local_models.answer: A custom OpenAI-compatible provider with its own baseURL can point at a locally hosted server; no first-party local-model runtime or Ollama adapter is documented.

account_switching.answer: Several accounts per provider form a pool; accounts assigned to a person are preferred for their runs and an account at its limit is sidelined for another eligible account.

vendor_account_requirement.answer: No Open Session account is needed; only model-provider accounts or keys, plus a GitHub App if GitHub features are wanted.

provider_restrictions.answer: Docs describe the xAI proxy minimum Grok CLI version (HTTP 426) and an opt-in fixed-subscription policy for shared sessions; provider terms about shared-server use of subscriptions are not discussed.

limitations: Provider terms for reusing subscriptions on a shared server are not stated in the docs read; the xAI path depends on a proxy that rejects old Grok CLI versions with HTTP 426.

claims.answer: One-line install.sh to a running per-user service, then add a model account, pick a repository and prompt; scratch sessions need no repo, a server-only repository needs no remote, GitHub is via an App. No managed cloud; BYO host install is first class (installer flags, EC2 guide).

scope.plan: Open source (MIT), self-hosted; no hosted plan

first_task_setup.answer: curl install.sh, open the printed URL, add a model account in Providers, pick a repo, write a prompt; `opensession doctor` verifies; budget 5 to 15 minutes.

no_git.answer: Scratch sessions (code mode with no repo) get a plain working directory; scratch workspaces have no project.

local_git_without_remote.answer: A repository created "This server only" has a bare origin beside the checkout; worktrees, diffs and local review work, with no GitHub PR flow.

hosted_git.answer: GitHub through a GitHub App (webhooks, PR agent, per-user sign-in) and code.storage as an alternative host.

prerequisite_guidance.answer: Requirements list curl, git, Bun for source installs, claude/codex CLIs, optional Tailscale, Daytona/Boat; doctor command checks readiness.

managed_cloud_setup.answer: No vendor-managed cloud exists; the sandbox providers are the customer's own Daytona/Boat/Modal accounts.

byo_vps_onboarding.answer: install.sh with --tailscale/--caddy/--cloudflare and a provisioning guide for a clean EC2 box (docs/setup/ec2.md).

limitations: Partly met or absent atomic parts: managed_cloud_setup; see each atomic answer for the limitation.

claims.answer: Admin CLI, a Bearer/cookie-authenticated REST and WebSocket surface used by the clients, inbound webhooks and an MCP surface only for sessions the server starts; no published API reference, SDK or externally exposed MCP server.

scope.plan: Open source (MIT), self-hosted; no hosted plan

cli.answer: `opensession` manages the service, repos, team, runners, integrations, automation recipes, plugins and packages; no run/steer/stop commands.

api.answer: Clients speak REST and WebSocket to the server with Bearer tokens (CLIENTS.md); routes exist for sessions, issues, automations, goals, etc., but no public reference was found (bounded search for openapi/swagger found none).

sdk.answer: Protocol package is a private workspace package exported as TypeScript source, not published (packages/core/protocol/README.md); the Subscription Gateway package is private and unfinished; no SDK found.

mcp_server.answer: In-process opensession-* MCP servers are handed to agent runs the server starts (sessions, goals, admin); none is offered to external agents (searched mcp-relay and routes: loopback relay only).

webhooks.answer: Inbound signed webhooks for GitHub, Slack, Linear, Plain and Stripe on the separate public ingress; automations can fire on external events.

operations.answer: Create, inspect, steer, stop and review sessions are available through the clients' REST/WebSocket surface; the CLI covers administration only.

authentication.answer: Opt-in GitHub sign-in (HttpOnly cookie or Bearer token); per-organization Bearer tokens in Chrome/Swift clients; default install has no authentication.

stability.answer: Version 0.4.x with no API stability statement found; ADR notes extension formats are data-only for now.

limitations: The REST/WebSocket API is internal to the clients with no documented contract or stability promise; the CLI cannot create or steer sessions.

claims.answer: MCP client with stdio and HTTP/OAuth servers, per-user allowedUsers scoping, MCP feeds as projects, skills (SKILL.md), recipes and a data-only package format; Pi's own plugins/extensions stay off.

scope.plan: Open source (MIT), self-hosted; no hosted plan

mcp_client.answer: Any MCP server added in Connections or mcp-config.json becomes tools; config is watched and reloads without restart; OAuth discovery and relay for HTTP servers.

plugins.answer: A data-only package format (MCP entry, feed, automation, skill) is implemented; docs/plugins.md describes a larger plugin runtime that is still a design doc.

custom_tools.answer: In-process opensession-* servers in mcp-catalog.ts and any MCP server.

instructions_import.answer: AGENTS.md and skills loaded from the session checkout's .claude/skills and .agents/skills plus shipped skills; host-account skills are disabled.

authentication.answer: Servers carry their own credentials; OAuth grants per user or workspace; automation runs get only the workspace grant unless mcpRunAs.

permission_scope.answer: Per-server allowedUsers; per-automation mcpServers allowlist; deny-sets stripped before Pi registers tools.

integration_owner.answer: Open Session owns the MCP client and credential projection; individual servers own their tools.

limitations: Partly met or absent atomic parts: plugins; see each atomic answer for the limitation.

claims.answer: Web UI (React, served by Bun server), Electron 43.2.0 macOS shell around the web UI, native SwiftUI app (iOS/macOS), Chrome MV3 extension; the shell renders the server frontend.

scope.plan: Open source (MIT), self-hosted; no hosted plan

desktop_implementation.answer: Electron shell (electron 43.2.0) wrapping the web UI plus a native SwiftUI macOS target.

mobile_implementation.answer: Native SwiftUI iOS app ("not a web view") and the PWA of the web UI.

hybrids.answer: Electron adds macOS window materials, Dock, deep links and an Apple Speech helper around the web frontend.

implementation_evidence.answer: CLIENTS.md plus packages/clients/mac/package.json and packages/clients/ios/project.yml at the pinned commit.

claims.answer: Sessions start from the web UI prompt, Slack mentions, GitHub issue labels/Issues page, Linear agent assignments, Plain tickets, feeds from any MCP list tool, automations and Chrome page context; external trackers stay authoritative.

local_creation.answer: New session in the web UI, drafts and a Desk todo list.

prompt_intake.answer: Prompt composer plus Slack, Chrome extension capture, automations and goals.

external_import.answer: GitHub open issues list with start button, Linear assignments, Plain tickets and MCP-backed feed projects whose items open workspaces.

chat_git_triggers.answer: Slack messages, GitHub `os` label, PR webhooks and mentions start or resume sessions.

authoritative_tracker.answer: The external system (GitHub, Linear, Plain) remains authoritative; feed items are things that already exist elsewhere.

stable_ids.answer: Feed items resolve to a workspace through a generic external reference so the same ticket reopens the same workspace.

sync.answer: Linear: planning moves the issue to Ready and implementation to In Progress; GitHub: os label added; no general bidirectional field sync.

supported_edits.answer: Status moves on Linear and labels on GitHub PRs (label_pull_request tool); other tracker fields are not edited by documented paths.

external_roundtrips.answer: Editing, prioritising and discussing issues requires the external tracker.

limitations: External tracker remains the system of record; sync is limited to documented status moves and labels; no two-way editing of issue fields.

plans.answer: Agent-written plans in the transcript, session todos (opensession-todos) and the coordinator's coordinator-summary.md; Linear flow offers a plan path before implementation.

acceptance_criteria.answer: Bounded search of docs and server for "acceptance criteria" found only prompt text, no structured field.

editors.answer: Humans edit by prompting or steering; session assets can be read and written by agents and viewed in the UI.

revisions.answer: Assets and git history keep revisions of files; no plan revision history is defined.

implementation_links.answer: Sessions link to branches, PRs and commits; plan items are not linked.

amendment.answer: Steers and queued prompts amend work while a turn runs.

restart_persistence.answer: Transcripts, queues and session state are stored by the session kernel and survive service restart.

limitations: No durable human-editable task plan with acceptance criteria; plans live in transcripts, assets and todos.

claims.answer: Workspaces group sessions; a coordinator spawns child threads (spawn depth capped) shown by state; goals pursue one session over days; no epics, blockers or enforced dependencies.

epics.answer: Searches for "epic" across packages, docs and scripts found no epic concept.

hierarchy.answer: Project to workspace to session, plus parent-child sessions via spawn_task/create_session; spawn depth is capped.

blockers.answer: Thread panel groups by blocked, ready to ship, working, idle, shipped; wait_for lets a session wait on timer, PR checks, workflow run or another session turn; no declared blocker links.

readiness.answer: Ready-to-merge and needs-input lanes derived from PR and ask state.

enforcement.answer: No dependency enforcement between tasks found (bounded search for dependsOn/blockedBy hit only a PR stack field and unrelated UI state).

state_propagation.answer: A coordinator is woken when its threads finish and keeps a summary; no automatic parent state rollup.

task_to_epic.answer: A conversation can be switched into coordinator mode later without recreating the workspace.

identity_retention.answer: The workspace and its sessions keep identity, transcript and branches when coordinator mode is toggled.

workflow_constraints.answer: No rigid workflow is required; mode ask/code/scratch and coordinator mode are optional settings.

limitations: No epic entity or dependency graph; PR stacks have a blocked indicator; wait_for can wait on a session turn.

takeover_continuity.answer: Memory checkouts and prompt prefix snapshots persist across sessions and people on the same server.

external_knowledge.answer: opensession-web tools web_search, fetch_url, read_page and any MCP server.

multimodal_inputs.answer: Images and video attachments, Chrome screenshots, voice dictation and OPENSESSION_IMAGE/VIDEO lines in transcripts.

freshness.answer: Ask checkouts refresh at most every five minutes; web tools fetch live; feed items cached about 60 seconds.

access_scope.answer: MCP allowlists, per-user servers and repository read tokens scope retrieval.

api_retrieval.answer: Agents call external MCP/API tools; no first-party API documentation indexer found.

citations.answer: Memory entries carry source links; transcript tool cards show inputs; no citation enforcement.

idea_parking.answer: Drafts and the Backlog lane hold sessions that are not started; Desk todos.

explicit_dispatch.answer: Starting a draft or sending the first prompt dispatches; suggest_task proposes work without starting it.

metadata.answer: Workspace goal, branch(es), PR, collaborators, reviewer, creator and times.

durable_states.answer: Running, waiting on you, idle, ready to merge, shipped derived and persisted by the session kernel.

claims.answer: Many sessions and workspaces run concurrently as detached run hosts (default admission cap 128 active) with resource-aware admission; the sidebar shows running, needs input, ready to merge and backlog lanes.

concurrent_sessions.answer: Each session turn runs as its own detached run host; the gateway admits up to OPENSESSION_RUN_HOST_MAX_ACTIVE (default 128).

concurrent_tasks.answer: spawn_task children, workflows and script runs run alongside the parent; workflow runner enforces concurrency limits.

quotas.answer: Documented numeric limits: run-host max active 128, memory headroom 4096 MB, CPU pressure 85 percent, admission timeout 900 s; no per-user quota.

observed_concurrency.answer: This catalog does not measure runtime concurrency; the repository ships memory-bench but no published concurrency figures. Business/benchmark fact, not readable from code.

status_visibility.answer: Sidebar lanes (Needs input, In progress, Ready to merge, Backlog), live thread cards and a Threads tab grouped blocked/ready/working/idle/shipped.

duplicate_prevention.answer: The same external ref reopens the same workspace; session mutation lock; webhook automations default to one run at a time (maxConcurrent).

evidence.title: GitHub repository metadata
evidence.finding: Repository tellahq/opensession: 424 stars, MIT license, not archived, default branch main, homepage opensession.com.

evidence.title: Open Session README
evidence.finding: Self-hosted agent-infrastructure server with web UI plus Slack, Linear, Plain and GitHub agents driving Pi-engine sessions in git worktrees or sandboxes; multiple Codex and Claude subscriptions and model APIs; install.sh quickstart; five clients; MIT.

evidence.title: Concepts
evidence.locator: Projects, Workspaces, Sessions, Automations, Goals, Coordinator mode, Workflows
evidence.finding: Defines project/workspace/session model, ask/code/scratch modes, steer and queue, coordinator threads, automations, goals, workflows, script runs, reports and databases, huddles, comments.

evidence.title: The clients
evidence.locator: Client table; Web UI; PWA; Electron; Swift; Chrome
evidence.finding: Web UI, PWA, macOS Electron shell, native Swift iOS/macOS app (TestFlight workflows, Xcode build) and Chrome extension (side panel, not on the Web Store).

evidence.title: Setup overview
evidence.finding: Linux, macOS or WSL2 server; no authentication by default (bind address is the boundary); opt-in GitHub sign-in; least-privilege run environment.

evidence.title: Pi engine
evidence.locator: Configure model access; Defaults and fallbacks; Isolation and restarts
evidence.finding: Pi is the only engine; Claude and ChatGPT account pools, SuperGrok accounts and API-key providers; fallback chain; detached run hosts survive gateway restart on Linux system scope.

evidence.title: Generated engine catalog
evidence.finding: Generated routing table: every known model id routes to pi/<provider>/<model>; mid-turn steer supported.

evidence.title: In-process MCP tool catalog
evidence.locator: Servers table; opensession-sessions; opensession-admin; opensession-goals; opensession-runners
evidence.finding: 38 in-process MCP servers, 187 tools, including spawn_task, task_status, send_to_session, cancel_task, set_session_reviewer, wait_for, create_automation and goals; run-class gating.

evidence.title: Security model
evidence.locator: Automation least-privilege; Fixed-subscription sessions; GitHub credential scoping; Per-user MCP servers
evidence.finding: Tool/env/credential-layer enforcement, MCP allowlists, deny-sets, minimal run environment, credential scoping, per-user MCP servers, sandbox allowlists.

evidence.title: Worktrees and disk
evidence.finding: Code workspaces get isolated git worktrees; ask is read-only on a shared checkout; attached repos; setup timeouts; publicationMode per repository.

evidence.title: Self-hosting sandboxes
evidence.locator: Setup; Where the agent runs; Sleep and wake; Security posture
evidence.finding: Optional per-session Daytona, Boat, use.computer, Mac VM or Modal machines; agent loop and credentials stay on the server; sleep/wake with durable disk; provider-owned compute.

evidence.title: Runners
evidence.finding: Runners are trusted persistent machines paired with opensession runner connect that receive bounded commands; Linux, macOS, Windows, ChromeOS.

evidence.title: Extending Open Session
evidence.locator: MCP servers; Feeds; Recipes; Integrations; Providers; Skills
evidence.finding: Any MCP server becomes tools; allowedUsers scoping; feeds map MCP list tools to projects; automation recipes; skills; plugins.

evidence.title: Plugins
evidence.finding: Plugin and package model for adding server and client capabilities.

evidence.title: Instance configuration
evidence.finding: Team roster, repositories, branding, integrations in ~/.opensession/config.json; client server defaults; Live Activities; APNs optional.

evidence.title: GitHub setup
evidence.locator: GitHub App; Force merge; Review options and rules; Approval gate; Per-user GitHub auth
evidence.finding: GitHub App with webhook intake, PR agent, review options (.os-review.json), approval gate check run, force-merge card pinned to head SHA, per-user sign-in.

evidence.title: Linear agent setup
evidence.finding: Linear agent-session assignments become sessions for the default repo; plan/implement paths; status names Ready and In Progress; opens PR with gh.

evidence.title: Install guide
evidence.locator: Fastest path; Onboarding; config.json; Service; Updates
evidence.finding: install.sh installs compiled release, user service, doctor/status/update commands, Windows through WSL2.

evidence.title: Networking
evidence.locator: Two separate connections; Tailscale; Public ingress is separate
evidence.finding: Private app on 3850 via Tailscale/SSH tunnel; separate fail-closed public ingress on 3860 for webhooks and sandbox callbacks.

evidence.title: Misc integrations
evidence.locator: Web push; Voice; Account health; Stripe approvals
evidence.finding: Web push with generated VAPID keys, voice dictation, account health, Stripe two-party approvals.

evidence.title: Memory repositories
evidence.finding: Git-backed agent memory repositories (team, user, channel) in Agent Memory Repo format; daily consolidation; injected into prompts with 6 KB budget.

evidence.title: MIT License
evidence.finding: MIT license text for the repository.

evidence.title: Security policy
evidence.finding: Private vulnerability reporting; operator guidance: keep off public internet, scope automations, treat Runner as shell.

evidence.title: Screenshots
evidence.finding: Screens are captured from an isolated synthetic demo instance with fictional repo acme-todo and PR #128.

evidence.title: opensession CLI
evidence.finding: Subcommands onboard/setup, bind, team, repos, doctor, sandbox, start, stop, restart, status, memory, logs, service, update, integrations, automations, plugins, packages, connect, runner, runners, version; no session-creation command.

evidence.title: GitHub issues routes
evidence.finding: Lists open GitHub issues and starts or resumes a session for an issue as the signed-in person; the os label starts a run through the webhook.

evidence.title: Command policy
evidence.finding: Semantic command floor for unattended bash: deny, allow or require_approval rules after normalizing shell quoting; unattended code runs only; interactive runs untouched.

evidence.title: Model usage recording
evidence.finding: Per-request tokens and cost recorded per session actor and counted per day and model, forwarded from run hosts.

evidence.title: Analytics
evidence.finding: Analytics view aggregates audit log turns, kernel usage catalog (model, tokens, list-price), session creators and gh PR counts, read-only.

evidence.title: Agent waits
evidence.finding: Durable background waits (timer, PR checks, workflow run, session turn); default session-turn wait timeout 2 hours.

evidence.title: Session container ownership
evidence.finding: Labels podman/docker containers started by agent bash with opensession.session=<id> via PATH wrappers and stops them on archive; not a sandbox boundary.

evidence.title: Workspace collaborators
evidence.finding: Adds teammates as workspace collaborators so the row files into their sidebar and notifies them.

evidence.title: Open Session website
evidence.finding: Tella-operated site titled "Your team's control room for coding agents"; schema.org metadata states isAccessibleForFree true and links the MIT license; no pricing page.

evidence.title: Release v0.4.82
evidence.finding: Release published 2026-11-09 with macOS arm64 DMG and ZIP, darwin arm64/x64 and linux arm64/x64 server tarballs with SHA-256 sidecars; no Windows desktop artifact.

evidence.title: First-party demo screenshot
evidence.finding: Workspace view with status lanes, running session transcript and per-session cost on the synthetic demo instance.

evidence.title: Electron shell package
evidence.finding: Electron 43.2.0 desktop shell targeting macOS arm64 DMG/ZIP.

evidence.title: Swift app project
evidence.finding: XcodeGen project for the native SwiftUI app with iOS 26.0 and macOS 26.0 deployment targets.

evidence.title: Executor architecture
evidence.locator: Resource control; Gateway settings table; Failure behavior
evidence.finding: Detached run hosts in transient systemd units with admission checks (active count 128, MemAvailable, CPU PSI 85), cgroup slices with CPU weights, bounded backoff and visible timeout, failure table.

evidence.title: Goals
evidence.finding: Self-pacing goals with a 5-minute wake floor and optional maxWakes.

evidence.title: Webhook automation concurrency tests
evidence.finding: Webhook automations default to one run at a time and allow overlap up to a configured cap.

evidence.title: Repo lifecycle
evidence.finding: Repositories commit .agents/setup and .agents/portals.json so workspaces provision themselves and expose apps as Portals.

evidence.title: Frontend typing and presence
evidence.finding: Web client tracks who is typing and viewing a session.

evidence.title: Audit log
evidence.finding: One JSON line per event into a daily file under ~/.opensession-audit; an external agent can ship the files.

evidence.title: AI review guide
evidence.finding: Story-first PR guide split into sections, saved per PR keyed by per-file diff hashes, updated on push.

evidence.title: Review requests
evidence.finding: Reviewer picker flags a session into the reviewer's Needs review band with a push alert until cleared.

evidence.title: PR merge readiness
evidence.finding: Deterministic read-only merge verdict from live GitHub state, checks, review decision and rulesets.

evidence.title: Stacked PRs
evidence.finding: Reads GitHub stacked pull request chains (public preview) through GraphQL.

evidence.title: Commit to session lookup
evidence.finding: Finds the session that shipped a commit from the transcript.

evidence.title: Session builds and rollouts
evidence.finding: Shows CI workflow runs, jobs and continuous-delivery status for a session from GitHub webhooks.

evidence.title: Deploys
evidence.finding: Durable agent-published internal web apps as immutable version snapshots behind the same sign-in gate.

evidence.title: Subscription Gateway README
evidence.finding: Subscription Gateway package is described as future and private while its contract is built.
